annotations.text: SPAN = 2x the demodulator passband, so the shaded band is ALWAYS the middle half. rtl_fm runs narrowband at -s 16000 and wideband at -s 192000, so NFM/AM get a 32 kHz view and broadcast FM a 384 kHz one. The alternative was 2x the channel spacing (50 / 400 kHz) - it shows the adjacent channel but loses the fixed middle-half reference.

Why the strip earns its height: 6.2 kHz off a 25 kHz channel is inaudible as a fault - the audio just sounds thin - but half the signal sitting outside the shading is unmissable. The caret is amber and tapping Centre it retunes to the peak.
On the broadcast dial the same rule puts the neighbours exactly at the frame edges: 192 kHz half-span, 200 kHz raster. Tuning between two stations is then visible rather than guessed at.

SETTLED AND SHIPPED. deploy/sdr/demod.py demodulates the same I/Q the strip is drawn from - 10% of one core for narrow FM audio plus the full waterfall plus this strip - and listen.py now runs it. This artboard is the FALLBACK: if the box cannot open the dongle for its own samples it drops to rtl_fm, which demodulates out of reach, and the screen says so rather than leaving a gap.
